name: ECC
cost: Free. The optional ECC Pro GitHub App for private repos is from $19 per seat a month
works_with: Claude Code (best supported), Codex, Kimi Code, plus limited adapters for Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Zed, GitHub Copilot and others
short: A large pack of agents, skills, hooks and rules that makes your coding agent plan, test, review and keep notes between sessions.
what: ECC installs a working method into your coding agent: 68 agents, 293 skills and 94 legacy commands, plus hooks, rules, memory and the AgentShield security scanner. It makes the agent plan before it builds, check changes with tests, review its own work from a fresh context and turn repeated wins into reusable skills.
who: Developers who use a coding agent every day and want a full process set up in one go. It works best with Claude Code; other agents get partial support, so check the README's support table first. The README suggests starting with the one workflow you need.
needs: Node.js 18 or newer for the guided setup
Git and Claude Code 2.1 or newer on your PATH for the Claude plugin setup

steps.title: Run the guided setup
steps.text: This is the recommended path for Claude Code. It handles the plugin install, updates, scope and hook choices.

steps.title: Or use Claude Code's plugin commands
steps.text: Pick one install method per agent. Installing twice into the same agent duplicates skills, commands and hooks.

steps.title: Add the rule packs you want
steps.text: Plugins can't ship rules, so copy them in yourself. Start with `rules/common` plus one language you use.
steps.code:
git clone https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC.git
cd ECC
mkdir -p ~/.claude/rules/ecc
cp -R rules/common ~/.claude/rules/ecc/
cp -R rules/typescript ~/.claude/rules/ecc/  # replace with your stack

steps.title: In Codex
steps.text: Inside Codex, `$configure-ecc` runs the guided setup.
steps.code:
codex plugin marketplace add affaan-m/ECC
codex plugin add ecc@ecc

steps.title: Or install without hooks
steps.text: This keeps the rules, agents, commands and core workflows but leaves out the runtime hooks.

steps.title: Remove it later
steps.text: Run these from the project folder you installed from. Plugin users remove the plugin in Claude Code instead.
steps.code:
npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 uninstall --dry-run
npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 uninstall

try.label: From the README
try.text:
/ecc:plan "Add authentication"

Other starting points:
/code-review for a fresh-context review
/build-fix to repair a build
/context-budget to check how full the context is

watch: Install only from the sources the README lists: the GitHub repo, the npm packages ecc-universal and ecc-agentshield, the plugin ecc@ecc, the ECC Tools GitHub App and ecc.tools. The README warns that unofficial mirrors may contain malware.
Hooks run shell commands and MCP servers can hold credentials. The README says to treat both as executable configuration. Use the minimal profile if you don't want runtime hooks.
If you already stacked install methods, the README's Reset / Uninstall section gives the cleanup order.
In Codex, the native hooks need an explicit trust decision.
Support outside Claude Code is limited. Check the platform support table before expecting every feature.
